first_impression.reaction: Googled 'best time to get married in greece' expecting the usual 'May to October is magical' fluff. Instead the first line says any guide naming one month for everyone is guessing, and the second paragraph promises official station averages. I skipped to the FAQ, then the table. Real numbers, a named source, the data periods, and it even admits the Naxos page doesn't state its period. That's the stuff I can check myself. So I read most of it. I then checked the table against the prose, and one line doesn't match its own numbers.

journey.quote: When to get married in Greece has no single answer, and any guide that names one month for every couple is guessing.
journey.reaction: Good. Not pretending there's a magic month. That's the opposite of a sales pitch.

journey.quote: Once you have two or three months in mind, a [Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=best-time-to-get-married-in-greece&utm_content=primary) turns them into dates a venue can actually hold.
journey.reaction: Booking link before I've seen a single number. It's conditional, so minor, but evidence first, then the ask.

journey.section: How to read the weather figures
journey.quote: The Naxos page does not state its data period.
journey.reaction: Admitting a gap in your own source. That's the line that makes me trust the rest of the table.

journey.section: How to read the weather figures
journey.quote: HNMS has no station on Santorini, Mykonos or Paros. Naxos, at 3 metres above sea level, is the official station for the group, so figures here are labelled Naxos.
journey.reaction: Tells me exactly what the proxy is instead of slapping 'Santorini: 27°C' on it. Honest.

journey.section: Greece wedding weather by month, April to October
journey.quote: Each cell shows the average maximum temperature, then the average number of rain days.
journey.reaction: One table, five stations, seven months. This is the comparison spreadsheet I'd have built myself. Going straight in.

journey.quote: July is the driest month in the table.
journey.reaction: Checked it against your own table. Naxos is 0.4 in July and 0.3 in August, Rodos 0.2 against 0.1. August is drier at two stations, and Kerkyra is level. A page built on numbers can't get its own numbers wrong. Now I'm rechecking everything else.

journey.quote: The Naxos station records a prevailing north wind in every month, and its wind power reading rises from 10.3 in June to 13.3 in July.
journey.reaction: 10.3 what? Knots? Beaufort? Some index? A number with no unit tells me nothing, and it gets repeated for September and October.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, [Smartraveller](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/europe/greece) says heatwaves are frequent in Greece over the summer months and can cause heat exhaustion, heat stroke and death.
journey.reaction: Dated, sourced, and a company selling summer weddings telling me summer can be dangerous. Good.

journey.quote: The Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia lists 1 to 15 August (the Dormition of the Theotokos) and 29 August among the dates when marriages are not permitted.
journey.reaction: That's a real catch I wouldn't have known about. Exactly the kind of thing that blows up a booking later.

journey.quote: Those are the Archdiocese's dates in Australia. For a church wedding in Greece, ask your priest and the local Metropolis.
journey.reaction: Clear about the limit of the source rather than passing Australian dates off as Greek rules.

journey.quote: May and late September to October keep maximums in the low to mid 20s at most stations.
journey.reaction: The table only has whole-month averages, and September is 25 to 28°C. 'Late September' isn't something these figures can show. Small, but it's the kind of stretch I notice.

journey.quote: On Santorini, Santo Wines in Pyrgos says its Wine Tourism Center, beside the winery with a view over the volcano, is open all year round.
journey.reaction: Open to tourists all year isn't the same as taking weddings all year. It's used in the FAQ to answer a wedding question, and it doesn't.

journey.quote: Each venue sets its own season. Angsana Corfu's Oribu Garden runs from April to October and its Vertigo Sky Bar from mid-May to the end of September.
journey.reaction: The question asks what month 'most' venues open. Three examples, one of them a tasting centre, isn't 'most'. Either answer it or change the question.

journey.quote: Ask your venue about water temperature for your month, since the figures in this guide cover air, not sea.
journey.reaction: Honest that it doesn't know. Fine, but then the question is in the FAQ and not answered.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, matching your shortlisted months to venue availability, travel and guest stays, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'Fee agreed in writing before any work begins' is the right signal. Still doesn't tell me whether venues pay you, but that's a phone question.

journey.section: Plan your month with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Choosing the month is the first real decision, and it shapes everything after it: the ceremony time, the shade, the fallback plan and the dates your guests book.
journey.reaction: Bit of brochure voice at the end. Harmless. Skipped it.

unanswered_questions: What unit is the Naxos 'wind power reading' in, and what does 13 or 14 actually feel like for a clifftop ceremony?
Does Santo Wines take weddings all year, or only tastings? (venue detail, deferred)
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from venues or suppliers? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real Greek wedding you've planned in a shoulder month I can look at, with what the weather actually did and the actual budget?

turn_offs_found.quote: July is the driest month in the table.
turn_offs_found.why: It's contradicted by the table directly above it (Naxos and Rodos are drier in August). An unsupported claim on a page whose whole selling point is numbers is worse than on a fluffy page, because it makes me doubt the rest.

turn_offs_found.quote: Once you have two or three months in mind, a [Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=best-time-to-get-married-in-greece&utm_content=primary) turns them into dates a venue can actually hold.
turn_offs_found.why: A CTA before any evidence. It's soft and conditional, so minor, but I want the data before the ask.

turn_offs_found.quote: On Santorini, Santo Wines in Pyrgos says its Wine Tourism Center, beside the winery with a view over the volcano, is open all year round.
turn_offs_found.why: Used to imply a year-round wedding option when it only says the tourism centre is open. Feels like a fact stretched to fill a gap.

turn_offs_found.quote: Choosing the month is the first real decision, and it shapes everything after it: the ceremony time, the shade, the fallback plan and the dates your guests book.
turn_offs_found.why: Sales-copy wrap-up rather than information. Minor, it's the tone I skip.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the month-by-month table and the 'Which months suit your wedding' section
Her parents, the Orthodox closed dates list and the Smartraveller heat paragraph

cta_reaction.why: The page did more homework than the other two planners I'm comparing: official data, dated government advice, the church calendar, and 'fee agreed in writing'. The July/August slip dents it, and I'd still want to know whether venues pay them before I hand over details. I'd book a call once I've picked my months, not today.

top_3_changes: Fix 'July is the driest month in the table.' to match the table: Naxos (0.3) and Rodos (0.1) are drier in August, and Kerkyra is level. Something like 'July and August are the driest months in the table' would hold.

Give the Naxos 'wind power reading' a unit or a plain-English meaning, or drop the number and keep the trend. And reword 'May and late September to October keep maximums in the low to mid 20s' so it doesn't claim part-month detail the monthly averages can't show.

Tighten the venue FAQ: either answer what 'most' venues do or reword the question, and don't use the Santo Wines tourism-centre line as if it were a wedding season. Optionally move the primary CTA below the table so evidence comes first.

No invented brand facts; commission and real-budget questions placed in unanswered_questions as deferred

open_questions.question: Does the source pack define the unit for the HNMS Naxos 'wind power' figure, and does the Santo Wines source say anything about weddings rather than the tourism centre?
